maild

Maild serves JMAP, SMTP, IMAP, CalDAV and CardDAV. Its library builds the same runtime for the daemon and integration tests. Private crates provide mail authentication, rules and Bayesian classification; metadata storage uses the shared mds library.

Accounts can run Sieve delivery scripts, managed through the Bus or the optional TLS ManageSieve listener on port 4190. Off-site redirects and automatic Sieve replies are disabled until the operator allows the account domain.

The IMAP protocol support and conformance audit documents command behaviour, wire tests, capability negotiation and the CONDSTORE integration hook.

Properties

Maild uses the shared props library with its store, sqlite and router features. A SqliteStore named maild and a PropsRouter with service name maild own the account_overrides, accounts, aliases, domains, engine_config, retention, tls_identities and log namespaces. The namespace modules register their schemas, SQLite mappings and hooks during build_runtime; the logging library registers log through logging::props::register.

The router handles maild.props.* requests. Durable changes publish on maild.props.records.changed and maild.props.audit; replay and audit semantics, error tokens and the five __props_* SQLite table names follow the shared props contract unchanged. Account, alias and domain hooks reconcile the mail store after committed changes.

Every Bus caller can read and write properties, including secret fields. tls_identities is a materialised resolver view: its Bus mutations return validation_error for every caller; internal reconciliation refreshes it. Vtoken management, retention sweeps and Bayesian rebuilds accept every caller without operator lists or delegation envelopes. Retention still validates its armed account set, deletion windows, dry-run flag and sweep limits.

Submission accepts mesh requests with no from sender. Audit records use the broker peer when supplied, otherwise the stable actor bus; the typed request selects the sending account. Sender validation, size limits and operation replay protection still apply. Config loading ignores unknown keys, so existing files carrying removed operator lists continue to load.

Shared libraries

Maild uses bus::native_client::NodedClient and the Bus connection helpers. Its advertised commands are registered in the repository Bus registry and checked by tests/registry.rs. Incoming commands retain their connection generation; the typed port helper preserves the remote return code and parsed reply.

Configuration uses config::Dir::{Etc, Var} and config::path. The system file is <Etc>/maild/config.conf.mix; strict-data loaders return typed errors. All path-valued settings resolve mixos:<root>/<relative> through paths, including database, blob and MDS storage, spam and rule files/directories, inbound filters, legacy TLS/DKIM files, managed key roots and each TLS/DKIM identity's paths. database aliases database_path. Logical root escapes and unknown roots fail config loading; ordinary relative and absolute paths keep their meaning. Node-config fallback and in-process runtime construction use the same resolver. Node-wide mail settings use the typed config::node::NodeConfig fields, with the shared config::tls SNI resolver. Logging attaches the namespace returned by logging::props::register through logging::props::attach.

Build provenance comes from buildinfo and its MIXOS_* build variables. Mail filters use the shared mix interpreter with its json and serde features. DAV uses davproto and the mixos:rawICalendar and mixos:rawVCard keys; retired raw keys remain errors.

Metadata store

Mds is the storage interface. SqliteCasMds stores per-set metadata in SQLite, shares a content-addressable blob store, and emits notifications after transactions commit. The library supports verification, garbage collection, index rebuilding, statistics and set archive import/export.

The archive format retains its original v1 identifier for compatibility with existing exports. The GC quiescence override is MDS_GC_QUIESCENCE_SECS; it accepts integer seconds of at least five, with a default of 60 seconds.

Run cargo test -p mds on a build worker. The mem-store feature exposes an in-memory implementation for consumers' tests. _stress-helper enables the internal mds-stress-writer and its Unix SIGKILL recovery test; this helper is never installed.

Running and packaging

Maild ships as its own binary, as declared in tools/release_packages.mx. tools/package.mix includes the binary, service/socket units and sysusers declaration, and the vendored parser's licences in the server archive.

maild@INSTANCE.service requires noded@INSTANCE.service and reads the same <config>/session/INSTANCE.env file, including its MIXOS_NODE_CONFIG broker configuration. It runs as the maild account. The unit uses <config>/maild/config.conf.mix, creates StateDirectory=maild, and sets MIXOS_VAR=/var/lib/maild; configured TLS material must be readable by maild. The unit documentation URL points to this manual.

maild.service is the plain per-host form, for a host that runs the plain noded.service rather than per-session brokers. It reads <config>/maild/config.conf.mix, creates StateDirectory=mixos/maild mixos/jmap, and takes its data paths from the maild config. Data paths the config leaves unset default under <state>/jmap, and DKIM, TLS and rule state under <state>/maild; with ProtectSystem=strict only those two directories are writable. The sysusers declaration adds maild to the mixos-tls group (gid 510), which it shares with webd for the TLS keys.

Socket activation

Both service forms retain CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE under the decision's interim clause, so upgrading preserves config binds on privileged ports. Activation is available, but its per-host installation is not automatic.

The shipped socket templates have no active ListenStream and cannot bind until an operator or installer renders the host's configured addresses:

TemplateDescriptor nameConfig source
maild-smtp@.socketsmtpevery smtp_inbound address
maild-submissions@.socketsubmissionsevery smtp_smtps address
maild-imaps@.socketimapsevery imap_imaps address
maild-jmap@.socketjmaplisten

For maild@INSTANCE.service, render a drop-in for each selected protocol's maild-PROTOCOL@INSTANCE.socket. Copy all addresses for that protocol from the instance's config; an inherited protocol replaces all its config binds. For example, maild-smtp@INSTANCE.socket.d/listeners.conf contains:

[Socket]
ListenStream=
ListenStream=192.0.2.10:25
ListenStream=[2001:db8::10]:25

Service=maild@%i.service selects the matching instance. For plain maild.service, use the default socket instance and add Service=maild.service to each socket drop-in. No installer enables these examples or chooses loopback/public addresses. Enable the rendered socket instances explicitly during the host's planned service transition, after checking for conflicts with already-bound config listeners. Each uses FreeBind=yes. TLS material is required for submissions and imaps. JMAP, CalDAV and CardDAV share the jmap HTTP listener and its TLS config. There is no separate STARTTLS submission listener on port 587.

Maild consumes fd 3 onwards only when LISTEN_PID matches its process; LISTEN_FDS and LISTEN_FDNAMES must describe named listening TCP sockets. Several fds may share a protocol name. Unknown names, mismatched counts and non-listeners fail startup. The activation environment is cleared before the runtime or helpers start. Inherited listeners replace configured binds for that protocol; protocols without inherited sockets still use their configured addresses. STARTTLS requirements match the inherited socket's actual local address, just as they do a configured bind.

Only after every privileged listener has a working enabled socket, or has been moved to an unprivileged config port, install this service drop-in at maild.service.d/socket-capabilities.conf (or maild@INSTANCE.service.d/socket-capabilities.conf):

[Service]
CapabilityBoundingSet=
AmbientCapabilities=

Keep the capability until that host transition is complete. Removing it while any configured privileged listener still binds itself makes startup fail.

Uploading and sending with JMAP

Upload an RFC 5322 message to the session's uploadUrl, then call Email/import with accountId and an emails map. Each entry has blobId, non-empty mailboxIds, optional keywords (default {}) and receivedAt (a UTCDate, or null for the default). The default date comes from the most recent Received header, or the import time. ifInState checks the Email state before any writes. Responses contain per-entry created or notCreated results, with id, canonical blob id, thread id and byte size for each created email.

Duplicate content within an account is rejected atomically with alreadyExists and existingId, including concurrent imports and imports through different upload aliases. It leaves existing metadata and memberships untouched, even when a retry requests different mailboxes or keywords. Maild does not add memberships as a side effect of this rejection: a failed import must remain safe to retry. The current Email/set update path only supports single-mailbox moves; it cannot add memberships to a multi-mailbox email. Safe merging needs an atomic duplicate/membership operation with defined per-membership keyword handling, preserving IMAP-only flags and the existing quota rules. Until that operation exists, clients can use existingId for supported updates or moves, but membership union is unavailable. Missing or invalid blob, mailbox or keyword references produce invalidProperties; invalid MIME produces invalidEmail. Uploaded aliases and account-owned CAS blob ids are accepted, with account ownership checked. Parser unwinds are contained and returned as invalidEmail for that entry. The legacy Email/set create extension reports invalid MIME as invalidProperties on blobId, a standard SetError. Positive account mail quotas are checked inside the creation transaction; concurrent imports cannot exceed them. Upload staging does not consume mail quota. Unexpected storage failures return serverFail; a failed creation transaction leaves no email, memberships or state changes behind. These are the RFC 8621 §4.8 import semantics; the earlier placeholder's successful duplicate-create response was incorrect.

Submit the returned email id with EmailSubmission/set. This works without maild's legacy top-level blobId extension on Email/set create. The Email creation id can also be referenced as #draft by submission in the same request; mailbox creation ids resolve in import's mailboxIds. Implemented /set methods also resolve Id fields, update/destroy targets and mailbox parents, ordering dependent creates within one call. Unresolvable references produce per-entry errors. Wrongly typed create, update, destroy or ifInState arguments instead fail the whole method with invalidArguments before any stage runs. A non-null ifInState must match the initial state; otherwise the whole call returns stateMismatch without running any mutation stage. Create, update and destroy stages run in that order. A /set is not one transaction across those stages; concurrent requests may change data between them, and a later per-entry failure does not roll back earlier successes.

Submission onSuccessUpdateEmail and onSuccessDestroyEmail name submissions, including #id creation references. Under RFC 8621 §7.5, an action applies only when the corresponding submission operation succeeds in that invocation. An existing submission id without a successful operation, a reference from an earlier call, a failed creation or an unknown reference is ignored. Such entries do not produce errors in the implicit Email/set. Maild currently implements submission creation; submission updates and destruction remain unsupported and cannot trigger these actions. Successful actions return the implicit Email/set response with the same call id; any email patch errors name the actual Email id, never the submission reference. Explicit success actions suppress the legacy automatic move to Sent, so the client's mailbox patch applies to the original draft memberships. An optional request createdIds map seeds these references and is returned with the new ids. The Email app still uses that extension: it should upload, import into Drafts with $draft, then submit the created id (and handle import errors, including alreadyExists). This branch does not change the app. Broader existing JMAP projection gaps, including some address/header fields, remain separate work; this is not a claim of full JMAP conformance. Thread ids are fetched in one read per Email/get batch; a missing legacy thread row projects null. SQLite, blob reads and MIME parsing run off the async executor.
